title: Adopted affine-space adjunction and canonical exceptional base change
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, $S$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $d\in\mathbb N$. Suppose a positive integer killing $\Lambda$ is invertible on $S$. Put $a:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. On the ordinary unbounded small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], for every normalized Tate-twist datum [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $Ra_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] is left adjoint to $La^*(-)(d)[2d]$. Moreover, in every cartesian square of $a$ [def-pc-fibre-product] whose pulled-back projection is compactifiable and quasi-compact [def-asd-compactifiable, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the canonical exceptional base-change map [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] is invertible. These are exactly the two clauses of the adopted theorem affineSpaceAdjunction_baseChange; no Noetherian or quasi-separatedness hypothesis is made on $S$.

proof.text: The first clause is precisely the already declared source-library theorem nonempty_rightDerivedLowerShriek_adjunction_affineSpace for an arbitrary scheme, not the Noetherian-only Sheaf version attached to cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction. Introduce the two twist instances and apply that existing theorem. Its separate hole is unchanged by this delivery.

For the affine line, factor its projection as the standard open chart into the projective line followed by the proper projection. The chart is quasi-compact because its composite with the projective projection is the quasi-compact affine projection. It admits the open-immersion compactification. Apply isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap_of_comp: its open-immersion branch is already proved, and its projective branch is lem-asd-projective-line-exceptional-base-change. This is the private proved helper affineLineBaseChangeModel.

Induct on d, over a fixed arbitrary base S. In dimension zero the projection is an isomorphism and the existing open-immersion result applies. Identify dimension d+1 with the affine line over dimension d using the sum/reindex isomorphism. Its projection is the composite of that isomorphism, the affine-line projection and the dimension-d projection. Compactifiability of the factors and quasi-compactness of the second projections supply every hypothesis of the composition theorem. Pull the invertible exponent to the intermediate affine space. Apply the composition theorem twice, using the induction hypothesis, the affine-line helper and the open-immersion result for the isomorphism. This gives the private proved helper affineSpaceBaseChangeModel. Pair it with the first clause. No quasi-separatedness or affine-cover descent is used.

theorem affineSpaceAdjunction_baseChange (d : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{u}) [HasInvertibleExponent Λ S] :
    (∀ [HasTateTwist Λ] [HasTateTwist.IsNormalized Λ],
      Nonempty (rightDerivedLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin d); S) ↘ S) ⊣
        L(((𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin d); S) ↘ S))^*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]) ⋙
          twistShift Λ 𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin d); S) d)) ∧
    ∀ ⦃S' P' : Scheme.{u}⦄ {g : S' ⟶ S} {p' : P' ⟶ S'}
      {g' : P' ⟶ 𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin d); S)} (sq : IsPullback g' p' (𝔸(ULift.{u} (Fin d); S) ↘ S) g)
      [HasCompactification p'] [QuasiCompact p'],
      IsIso (rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap Λ sq)
